id: DF deltas on the map (owner, 8 Nov 2026: "I don't see why we couldn't have a Nile-like delta in our world, we shouldn't prevent it")
status: frozen before any delta area is joined to a discharge
why_not_height: a height rule (low land near a mouth) cannot find deltas on this map: its coasts sit at ~1 m by construction (plan_D1 closing_note). A delta is tied to a river's mouth and to the water it brings.
rule: every drawn river that ends at the sea or a lake builds a fan: land within r of its mouth, r = sqrt(2 A / pi) (a half disc of area A), A = a Q^b from the river's simulated mean discharge Q at the mouth; inside the fan the irrigable share is s_fan x exp(-H / 5 m) (H the height above the mouth's bed, the D2b gate); the map takes the larger of this and the river-distance rule

earth_data.deltas: Edmonds et al. 2020 (Nat. Commun. 11:4741, CC BY 4.0) supplementary table: river mouth point and geomorphic area of each delta (data/cache/deltas/edmonds2020_deltas.xlsx)
earth_data.discharge: HydroRIVERS v1.0 (Lehner & Grill 2013) DIS_AV_CMS of outlet reaches (NEXT_DOWN = 0); a delta takes the largest outlet discharge within 30 km of its river-mouth point; deltas without one >= 10 m3/s are left out and counted

fit: log10 A = log10 a + b log10 Q by least squares on the development deltas: Africa, Europe and Asia (river mouth east of 30 W, excluding Oceania: south of 10 S and east of 110 E)
check: held out: the Americas and Oceania. Reported: RMSE of log10 A against a constant (the development median) and the fit's own RMSE; the fit is used if it beats the constant on the held-out deltas, otherwise A = the development median for every river
s_fan: HID 1900 equipped share inside the Nile delta polygon (convex hull of the Edmonds points; development region of D2/D2b, not a blind pool); one number, reported with the dry-delta values it rests on
map: harvest/export.py geometry (Earth-fit atlas with a terrain file); simulated discharge from rotclimate.routing (rivers flow through open lakes, height map v2.2)

result_discharge_only.note: discharge alone explains ~20 % of the variance in delta area; the Nile is at about the 94th percentile for its discharge

amendment_1.by: owner choice ("Earth-fitted drivers"), after the discharge-only result

predictors.sediment: BQART pristine sediment load (Syvitski & Milliman 2007): Qs = w Q^0.31 A^0.5 R T for basin T >= 2 C, 2 w Q^0.31 A^0.5 R below, w = 0.0006 (Qs Mt/yr, Q km3/yr, A km2, R km, T C), B = 1; Earth: Q and A from HydroRIVERS (DIS_AV_CMS, UPLAND_SKM), R = highest reach head upstream minus the mouth, T = catchment-area-weighted mean of WorldClim 2.1 annual temperature at the reach heads (5 arc-min); map: the same from simulated discharge, routed upstream area, the height map and the model climate
predictors.exposure: share of 32 directions from the mouth whose open-water fetch reaches 1,500 km (land from WorldClim 5 arc-min on Earth, the map land mask on the map, the map edge counted as open sea)

candidates.M3: log10 A_delta ~ log10 Q + log10 Qs + exposure

amendment_1.selection: 5-fold cross-validated RMSE on the development deltas (Old World); the lowest wins
amendment_1.check: held-out Americas + Oceania once more (already used once for the discharge-only fit, so not fully unseen); reported against the discharge-only fit and the constant; the chosen model replaces the discharge-only rule if it beats it there
amendment_1.s_fan: unchanged (Nile HID 1900 share inside the Edmonds polygon)

amendment_1_result.bugs_fixed_before_this_result: WorldClim marks the sea as -32768 in elevation: the first exposure run saw no sea (all 0) and the land mask was fixed; a reader in my own command first printed a stale fit2.json
amendment_1_result.verdict: the drivers do not beat discharge alone on the held-out deltas (1.336 vs 1.283 log10 RMSE); BQART sediment load alone is worse than discharge (dev R2 0.08 vs 0.19); the discharge-only rule stays. Delta size on Earth is mostly not predictable from these global drivers: the Nile stays a ~94th-percentile delta for its discharge
